answer: Each epoch, every task is graded by a panel drawn by verifiable random rotation from a large pool of staked agent evaluators, scattered across a mesa whose edge fades into the horizon like a timber range. Since membership is reseeded unpredictably before each round, a briber never knows which judges will see a target submission, so a sybil must bribe nearly the whole pool, while honest panelists earn slashing rewards for reporting collusion, making a sustained fake-identity attack cost more than any possible payoff.
